title: Unfold a hand truck's nose-plate extension: hold its spring pop-pin out while folding the plate down
instruction: Unfold the nose-plate extension: pull the pin out and hold it, fold the plate down flat, then let go.
context: Unfolding a hand truck's nose-plate extension is a routine operation for laborers and freight, stock and material movers (about 3.0 million US workers, BLS OEWS May 2023). The difficulty is physical and bimanual: the extension is locked up by a spring pop-pin that runs along the hinge line through a lug on its edge, so one arm must hook the pin's T-handle and hold it pulled against its spring while the other pushes the plate over and down through a 90-degree arc; released too early, the pin springs back across the lug's path and stops the plate.
setup: Positions are measured on the table from the point midway between the two arm bases, which stand 61 cm apart: forward means away from the arms, left and right as seen from behind the arms. Nose plate (nose_plate, fixed): a hand truck's steel nose plate 17 x 19 cm, 3 cm thick, centred 31 cm forward on the centre line. Its red extension (plate joint), 14 cm long x 17 cm wide x 1 cm thick, is hinged along the nose plate's near edge (24 cm forward, 3.6 cm up) and stands folded straight up; a 6 mm lug on its left edge carries a 14 mm square hole 7 cm from the hinge. A zinc 10 mm square pop-pin (pin joint) runs left-right, along the hinge line, through a guide bracket on the frame and through the lug's hole, 2.5 cm in front of the standing extension and 10.6 cm up; its T-handle is on the outside, 14.8 cm left of centre, 3.5 cm from the bracket; a 40 N/m spring pushes it in and it draws out 2.5 cm to the left, clearing the lug. Nothing else is on the table.
scoring: The pin is pulled once it has been drawn at least 2 cm of its 2.5 cm travel; the plate is down when its hinge is within 3 degrees of flat. Score at the end of the trial: 0.3 once the pin has been pulled (at any time) plus 0.3 for the plate down (0 to 0.6). 1.0 when the plate is down, the pin has been let go (back within 5 mm of home), nothing moves and no gripper tool point is within 4 cm of the plate's middle or the pin's handle, held for 1 s (the trial then ends; completed less than 1 s before the run limit scores 0.6).
reset_notes: Fold the extension back up and let the pin spring back through its lug; the nose plate stays fixed.
fidelity: Approximate. The hand truck is reduced to its nose plate and extension (fixed to the table); the pop-pin is a sprung slide; plates and pin are rigid boxes and the lock works by contact between the pin and the lug on the extension's edge: the pin runs along the hinge line, so the lug cannot swing past it until the pin is drawn out. PhysX rigid-body contacts with default friction.
scores: Dream-1 run: 0.0 (pushed the extension about 2 degrees until the lug met the locked pin; pin never pulled; hit the 120 s step limit); demo: 1.0 (one arm drew the pop-pin out and held it while the other folded the extension down flat; pin released, hands clear, held 1 s)
